title: Orca Emoji (🫍): Codepoint, Meaning & Why It Isn't a Whale
meta_description: The orca emoji 🫍 (U+1FACD): its Unicode 17.0 codepoint, how to type it, which platforms draw it yet, and why Unicode files an orca beside the dolphins.
hero_tagline: The black-and-white orca 🫍 with its codepoint, its keyboard routes, the platforms that draw it so far, and the marine emoji people reached for before it existed. Click any symbol to copy it instantly.
intro: 🫍 ORCA (U+1FACD) arrived in Unicode 17.0 and reached most phones with iOS 26.4 in March 2026. Unicode files it under animal-marine, one shelf along from the dolphin rather than the whale, and that placement is taxonomically right: an orca is the largest of the dolphins, not a whale at all, despite "killer whale" being the name almost everyone types first. Until this codepoint existed, an orca had to be written as 🐋 or 🐬, and neither is the animal. This page gives the glyph, the input routes, and the near neighbours it is still confused with.
